name: Niederau
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny village in the Wildschönau-Tal – family-friendly and with direct access to the Wildschönau ski area.
beschreibung:
Overview

Niederau is the welcoming gateway village to the 24-kilometer-long alpine highland valley of the Wildschönau in the Kitzbühel Alps, within the Kufstein district, located roughly ten kilometers south of the railway junction town of Wörgl at an altitude of 828 meters. Home to around 1,150 residents, Niederau forms the first of four parish villages comprising the Wildschönau municipality, which encompasses around 4,420 people in total. The town is dominated by the striking 1,500-meter Markbachjoch and the 1,621-meter Lanerköpfl peaks. With its slender, pointed church spire visible from afar, traditional wooden farmsteads, and direct doorstep access to the gondola lifts, Niederau effortlessly blends rural alpine serenity with lively outdoor adventures. It holds global acclaim both as the birthplace of ski lift engineering in Tyrol and as a premier European flight school center for paragliding.

History

The earliest documented mention of a church in Niederau dates back to 1409. For centuries, the community ecclesiastical ties lay with the distant ancient parish of Söll, becoming an independent vicarage in 1631 and a full parish in 1891. The parish church of Saints Sixtus and Oswald retains a 13th-century Romanesque choir tower, a nave remodeled in Baroque style in 1740 by master builder Jakob Singer, and an impressive westward extension designed in 1970 by renowned Austrian architect Clemens Holzmeister; its patronage of Pope Saint Sixtus II is an ecclesiastical rarity in Tyrol. Niederau entered Alpine ski lore on January 14, 1947, when pioneer Sepp Hochmuth opened the Markbachjoch chairlift—the very first chairlift in Tyrol—igniting the modern winter sports era across the valley.

Getting There

Traveling to Niederau is swift and effortless. Motorists exit the A12 Inntal Autobahn at Wörgl Ost and follow the well-engineered L3 Wildschönauer Landesstraße winding gently uphill for ten kilometers into Niederau, with driving time from the motorway taking just ten minutes. Rail passengers arrive at Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, a major international rail hub served by Austrian Railjets, German ICEs, and EuroCity trains. From Wörgl station square, frequent VVT regional buses (route 4064) whisk travelers directly to Niederau village center in only 17 minutes. Holidaymakers holding the Wildschönau Card enjoy complimentary bus and ski shuttle travel throughout the valley.

Tips

In winter, the Markbachjoch gondola provides instant access to the sporty core of the Ski Juwel Alpbachtal Wildschönau ski area, featuring challenging black runs like the Hochberg downhill, deep-snow freeriding on the Lanerköpfl, and gentle beginner nurseries in the valley. In summer, the Markbachjoch is renowned as one of Europe's top paragliding havens thanks to reliable, wind-protected thermal air currents, with the famed Wildschönau Flight School offering tandem flights and pilot courses. A leisurely cultural walk follows the Franziskusweg trail to Oberau, lined with expressive bronze statues by artist Hubert Flörl. Be sure to visit the Schönangeralm at the head of the valley to sample award-winning cheeses at the alpine show dairy, or try the exhilarating toboggan run at Lanerköpfl.
